paragraphs.text: i.e., In the beginning of Zedekiah’s reign, as before, was this word uttered. Or rather, in those latter times forementioned, {Jer 30:24} after the return from Babylon, but especially in the days of the Messiah. The modern Jews vainly apply it to the coming of their Messiah, quem tantis etiamnum ululatibus exposcunt, whom they yet expect, but to no purpose.
paragraphs.anchor: At the same time

paragraphs.text: Of Pharaoh’s sword, who pursued them; and though he smote them not, because the Lord kept him off, yet he is said to have done it: {a} like as Balak afterwards "arose and fought against Israel," {Jos 24:9} he had a mind so to have done, but that he was overawed: he did not indeed, because he dared not.
paragraphs.anchor: The people that were left of the sword.

paragraphs.text: i.e., To the land of Canaan, after so long trouble and travel. I effected that then, though it were held improbable or impossible: so will I do this promised reduction of my people from Babylon.
paragraphs.anchor: When I went to bring him to rest

paragraphs.text: {a} Fieri dicitur quod tentatur aut intenditur.

This seemeth to be the people’s objection. {a} You tell us what was done of old; but these are ancient things, and little pertaining to us, who are now under a heavy captivity; iam refrixit et obsoleta videtur Dei beneficentia. Hereunto is answered,
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord hath appeared of old unto me.

paragraphs.text: I am one and the same. I am Jehovah that change not, whatever thou mayest think of me, because I seem angry at thy misdoings.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love.

paragraphs.text: Or, Therefore will I draw out lovingkindness towards thee. {as Psa 36:10} {See Trapp on "Psa 36:10"}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore with lovingkinduess have I drawn thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} Iudaeorum quiritantium verba. - Zeged.
See Jer 34:18.
paragraphs.anchor: Again I will build thee.

paragraphs.text: All shall be hail and merry with thee as heretofore: yea, thou shalt have spiritual joy, which is res severa, severe and solid, such as doth not only smoothe the brow, but fill the breast.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt be adorned with thy tabrets.

paragraphs.text: Profunda pax erit: nemo te perterrefaciet. Thou shalt have plenty, peace, and security.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt yet plant vines.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Shall have God’s good leave and liking so to do. Heb., Shall profane them, i.e., not abuse them, but use them freely, even to an honest affluence. See Lev 19:23. {See Trapp on "Lev 19:23"}
paragraphs.anchor: The planters shall plant them, and shall eat them as common things

paragraphs.text: Such as are set to keep those vineyards. {Jer 31:5}
paragraphs.anchor: The watchmen upon the mount Ephraim.

paragraphs.text: As the ten tribes first made defection, so shall they be forwardest in the reformation. England was the like alate.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall cry, Arise ye, and let us go up to Zion.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Neigh unto the heads of the nations, ut illa vobis adhinniant et pariter in Christi fide iubilent, that they may join joys with you, and help to make up the choir.
paragraphs.anchor: Shout among the chief of the nations.

paragraphs.text: The saints have never so much matter of praise, but that they may at the same time find cause enough to pray for more mercy. {Psa 18:3}
paragraphs.anchor: Publish ye, and praise ye, and say, O Lord, save.

paragraphs.text: Here is a present answer to such a prayer; and this promise hath its performance chiefly in the kingdom of Christ, who will not suffer the least or the weakest of his to miscarry. See Isa 35:5-6.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold, I will bring them.

paragraphs.text: Prae gaudio, inquit, flebunt, before happiness, it is said, they were weeping, they shall weep for joy, having first soaked themselves in godly sorrow by the spirit of grace and of supplications or deprecations poured upon them, {Zec 12:10} being solicitous about their salvation.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall come with weeping.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To the brooks of waters, i.e., to the holy ordinances. {as Psa 23:3}

paragraphs.text: I do all of free grace.

paragraphs.text: And therefore higher than the kings of the earth. {Psa 89:27}
paragraphs.anchor: Ephraim is my firstborn.

paragraphs.text: Hear and bear witness of the gracious promises that I make to my people; for I would have them noted and noticed.
paragraphs.anchor: Hear the word of the Lord, O ye nations.

paragraphs.text: Redemption is a voluminous mercy, an accumulative blessing.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath redeemed Jacob.

paragraphs.text: As those do who have not this contented godliness, but serve various lusts, to their great vexation.

paragraphs.text: Or, After their sorrow. I will turn all their sadness into gladness, their sighing into singing, their tears into triumphs, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: And make them rejoice from their sorrow.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Provide liberally for my ministers; {Isa 66:21} they and theirs shall be well maintained. Terms taken from the good and fat parts of the sacrifices, which were allotted for the priests.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will satiate the soul of the priests with fatness

paragraphs.text: It was once, when the poor captives were carried that way to Babylon, the mothers bitterly bewailing their Luctuosam faeunditatem. It was also another time, when Herod barbarously butchered the babes of Bethlehem. {Mat 2:16-18} But now the case is altered, joy is restored, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: A voice was heard in Ramah.

paragraphs.text: An elegant personification. {See Trapp on "Mat 2:18"}
paragraphs.anchor: Rachel weeping for her children.

paragraphs.text: Take up in time, O Rachel, and the rest; God comforteth the abject, {2Co 7:7} he restoreth comfort to his mourners. {Isa 57:18}
paragraphs.anchor: Refrain thy voice from weeping.

paragraphs.text: Or, For thy posterity. Tribulation causeth patience, and patience experience, and experience hope; lively hope, such as maketh not ashamed, is not disappointed, Spes in fundo. Hope in the depths. God can recompense his people’s patience and obedience, in their heirs and executors.
paragraphs.anchor: And there is hope in the end.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Hearing I have heard; his moans and laments have rung in mine ears. So Hos 14:8, "I have heard him, and observed him." This is God’s speech concerning the Christian Church of the Jews; for in this sermon we may easily observe a frequent change of persons, tanquam in opere dramatico, as in an interlude.
paragraphs.anchor: I have surely heard Ephraim bemoaning himself.

paragraphs.text: i.e., I was chastised to good purpose, taught my duty. {as Psa 94:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast chastised me, and I was chastised

paragraphs.text: Give me the whole turn, that I be not as an untamed sturdy heifer, or as a cake half baked.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn thou me.

paragraphs.text: After that I had turned short again upon myself, as those penitents, {1Ki 8:47} as Manasseh, the publican, {Luk 18:13} and that prodigal. {Luk 15:17}
paragraphs.anchor: Surely after that I was turned, I repented.

paragraphs.text: Postquam ostensum fuerit mihi. {a} After that I knew myself, or rather was made known to myself - scil., by mine afflictions sanctified; for Schola crucis, schola lucis. The followers of the cross are the followers of light. Afflictions are those pillulae lucis, that serve notably to clear the soul’s eye sight.
paragraphs.anchor: And after that I was instructed.

paragraphs.text: {b} Sicut mulierculae in puerperio facere solent, saith Luther, as travailing women use to do. It is a token of greatest grief. See Eze 21:12.
paragraphs.anchor: I smote upon my thigh

paragraphs.text: Abashed and abased to the utmost; my sorrow was deep and downright.
paragraphs.anchor: I was ashamed, yea, even confounded.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The brunt and burden of my reproachful practices in my youth. See Job 13:26 Psa 25:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Because I did bear the reproach of my youth

{b} Homer hath it oft πεπληγετο μηρω, he smote on his thigh. Cicero hath the like, lib. iii. Tuscul.

q.d., Ay sure he is; and never more dear and pleasant than when thus beblubbered; like as some faces appear most oriently beautiful when they are most enstamped with sorrow. Heb., Is he a child of delight? q.d., He may seem to be otherwise by my hard dealing with him; but so he is assuredly - "Behold, he whom thou lovest is sick." {Joh 11:3}
paragraphs.anchor: Is Ephraim a dear son? is he a pleasant child?

paragraphs.text: Or, So oft as I speak of him, I am mindful still of him. See Isa 49:14; Isa 49:16.
paragraphs.anchor: For since I spake against him, I do earnestly remember him still.

paragraphs.text: Perstrepunt viscera mea. My bowels work, as that mother’s did toward her child; {1Ki 3:26} as Croesus’ dumb son’s did, when seeing a fellow ready to kill his father, he burst out into, Kill not king Croesus. {a} See Hos 11:8. {See Trapp on "Hos 11:8"}
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore my bowels are troubled for him.

paragraphs.text: {a} Aνθρωπε, υη κτεινε τον Kροισον. - Herod.

Statue tibi statuas Mercuriales - q.d., I will surely bring thee back by the same way thou wentest hence into captivity; therefore take good notice of the way now, that thou mayest know it again another time. This God saith to quicken their faith, and to ascertain them of his love and favour; which is not like the winter sun, which casteth a goodly countenance when it shineth, but giveth little heat and comfort, &c. We must also set up waymarks, observe how we fell from the Lord, repent and do our first works.
paragraphs.anchor: Set thee up waymarks.

paragraphs.text: This is done, saith Augustine, when God is sought for God’s sake. Sed vix diligitur Iesus propter Iesum, saith the same Father; but this is rarely done.
paragraphs.anchor: Set thine heart towards the highway.

paragraphs.text: Hunting after human helps, and - refusing to set thy heart on the right straight way {Jer 31:21} - fetch a compass, to thy loss of time and labour.
paragraphs.anchor: How long will thou go about?

paragraphs.text: Who wast at times O virgin of Israel. {Jer 31:21}
paragraphs.anchor: O thou backsliding daughter.

paragraphs.text: Or, Will create; he is even about it.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Say some, the Jews (who are now looked upon as weak women, and may say Imbelles damae, quid nisi turba sumus?). shall compass about, and conquer the Chaldees, those men of might - Sicut hostis circundat hostem. Or, As others sense it, the Church Christian, how weak soever at first it may seem, and inconsiderable, yet shall be able, by the confession of her faith, to resist her most potent persecutors, and by faith to overcome them, {1Jn 5:4} as she did in the apostles, {Act 4:13-14; Act 4:33; Act 5:18-19; Act 5:38-42} in the noble army of martyrs and confessors. The text is generally understood to be Christ’s wonderful conception in the womb of his virgin mother.
paragraphs.anchor: A woman shall compass a man.

paragraphs.text: Et haec pertinent ad regnum Christi propriissime. These words also, to the end of the chapter, do most properly pertain to the kingdom of Christ, saith Oeecolampadius.
paragraphs.anchor: Thus saith the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: Or, Yet again. {as Jer 31:5}
paragraphs.anchor: As yet.

paragraphs.text: This prayer is daily made for the Church by all her children.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord bless thee.

paragraphs.text: Agricolae et pecuarii; the citizens of the Church shall be plain hearted and profitable persons, living together in amity, and not jarring, as husbandmen and shepherds oft do; Cain and Abel for instance.
paragraphs.anchor: Husbandmen, and those that go out with flocks.

paragraphs.text: Or, I will satiate, fill them with my fulness, so that they shall have enough for their own, and not emulate others. A good man shall be satisfied from himself, {Pro 14:14} as knowing within himself that, whatever he hath here, little or much, he hath in heaven a better and more enduring substance. {Heb 10:34}
paragraphs.anchor: For I have satiated the weary soul.

paragraphs.text: Out of my prophetic dream.
paragraphs.anchor: Upon this I awaked.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The promises (Christ in the promises) were sweet unto me, and I was as much refreshed therewith, as with sound sleep after hard toil or travel.
paragraphs.anchor: And my sleep was sweet unto me

paragraphs.text: I will repeople the country, and raise up many believers to Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: I will sow the house of Israel.

paragraphs.text: I have been sedulous and assiduous.
paragraphs.anchor: Like as I have watched over them.
To pluck up and break down, &c.

paragraphs.text: I will make them a plentiful amends.
paragraphs.anchor: So I will watch.

paragraphs.text: There shall be rectius de operibus Dei iudicium, a more correct judgment passed upon God’s proceedings. See about this byword, Eze 18:2.
paragraphs.anchor: In those days they shall say no more.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Every unbeliever shall: neither shall the gospel save him.
paragraphs.anchor: But every one shall die for his own iniquity

paragraphs.text: The same for substance with the former made with Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and the Israelites in the wilderness; but new in respect of the form thereof, the manner of dispensing it - viz., more clearly, freely, effectually, and spiritually now under the gospel, than in those days of yore, when they saw the face of God only in that dark glass of the ceremonies; whereas we, with open face, &c. {2Co 3:18}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make a new covenant.

paragraphs.text: Not so, but a great deal better, in regard of larger measures of the Spirit now poured out upon all flesh: together with the efficacy thereof in the hearts of God’s covenanters, who have a duplicate of God’s law written within them. {Jer 31:33} Lex iubet, gratia iuvat: hence it is an "everlasting covenant," and the fruits of it are "sure mercies," "compassions that fail not," as is here set forth.
paragraphs.anchor: Not according to the covenant.

paragraphs.text: This the apostle calleth the "law in their minds," opposed to the "law of their members"; {Rom 7:23} for the natural man is inversus decalogus, oposed to the law, "he is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be." But God putteth into the hearts of his people the counterpart of his holy law; he stamps, as it were, a decalogue upon their spirits; he puts into them an inward aptness, answering the law of God without, as the lead answereth the mould, wax the seal, as tally answereth tally: or as indenture indenture.
paragraphs.anchor: I will put my law in their inward parts.

paragraphs.text: This promise is divini mellis alveare, as one calleth it, The hive of heavenly honey.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

paragraphs.text: Deest coactio, non deerit cohortatio. {a} Men shall learn with much less ado, because "taught of God," and lively illightened by his Holy Spirit: et quando Christus magister, quam cito discitur quod doeetur? saith Augustine; when Christ becomes a man’s teacher, he must needs be a forwardly scholar. Some make this to be the sense of the words, that in gospel times the truths of Christ, and the knowledge of the Son of God, should be so evident, that men might get more of themselves without a teacher, than with one in the legal administrations; as Paul also showeth, 2 Cor. iii. Not that men should have no need of teaching at all in those times; for the best know but in part, and must daily grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ. {2Pe 3:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour.

paragraphs.text: All mine elect shall know me in some competent measure: know the principles, {Heb 6:1-2} and go on unto perfection, ib.
paragraphs.anchor: For they shall all know me.

paragraphs.text: In heaven, and in their own consciences also, {Zec 3:4} provided that they put this and the like promises in suit by their prayers. {Mal 3:16} Augustine, Mr Perkins, and Archbishop Ussher expired with crying for mercy and forgiveness.
paragraphs.anchor: For I will forgive their iniquities.

For their better security and settlement; he borroweth a comparison from the surest things, sun, sea, &c.

paragraphs.anchor: Which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar.

paragraphs.anchor: If those ordinances depart from before me.

paragraphs.anchor: Behold the days come, saith the Lord, &c

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem shall be re-edified, the Church eternally re-established by Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: That the city shall be built to the Lord.
From the tower of Hananeel.
Unto the gate of the corner.

paragraphs.text: Versus collem scabiosi, toward the hill of the scabby, so Tremellius rendereth it; and Junius thinks it was so called because thither they used to send their lepers and lazars. {poor and diseased person} At Geneva in times of Popery there, they had in an empty place certain cottages set up whereunto they sent their lepers, wherewith that city then abounded, through the horrible filthiness that was there in those days committed. But from the year 1535, wherein they embraced the purity of the gospel, there hath been not above one leper seen in that city. So testifieth Matthaeus Cottherius in his Exposition of the Revelation, printed at Sedan in France, A.D. 1625.
paragraphs.anchor: Upon the hill Gareb.

paragraphs.text: alias Golgotha, as some think, but these places here mentioned, as also those Zec 8:3; Zec 14:4, as they were known to the ancients, so to us at this day they are unknown. Travellers tell us that Jerusalem is now a poor obscure place, governed by a Turkisk Sanzak, and that Golgotha, or Calvary, is in the very midst of the town.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall compass about to Goath

paragraphs.text: Of Rephaim, say some; of Tophet, say others. See on Jer 31:39.
paragraphs.anchor: And the whole valley of the dead bodies.

paragraphs.text: So is the holy Catholic Church, the New Jerusalem which is above especially.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be holy unto the Lord.

paragraphs.text: This cannot be applied to the earthly Jerusalem, which was plucked up and thrown down by the Romans once and again; but especially by Aelius Hadrian the emperor, who laid the whole country waste almost, drove the Jews utterly out of it, set a sow of white marble over the chief gate of Jerusalem in reproach of their religion, and called the city by his own name, Aelia, commanding the Jews not once to look towards it from any tower or hill. It must be therefore meant to be the Church, which cannot be ruined.
paragraphs.anchor: It shall not be plucked up nor thrown down any more for ever.
